item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Tehran Says It Is Reviewing U.S. Proposal as Trump Makes New Threats
item.summary: An Iranian official said his government was looking at an American plan to end the war, hours after President Trump threatened to resume strikes. Earlier Wednesday, another Iranian official dismissed a reported proposal as a “list of American wishes.”

item.title: In Talks With Iran, China Calls for Opening of Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: China’s top diplomat also warned against the restarting of hostilities as he met with Iran’s foreign minister. The U.S. has urged China to pressure Iran to reopen the waterway.

item.title: Iran’s Oil Sector and Economy Are Under Pressure as U.S. Blockade Bites
item.summary: Tehran says it can endure the pain, but its oil may soon have nowhere to go.

item.title: In Romania, Living With Weapons of War Spilling Into NATO Territory
item.summary: Four years of battle in Ukraine is taking a toll on neighboring Romanians. Even if the war has not crossed the border, drones have done so.

item.title: Reclaiming the Name of the Black Hero Who Inspired ‘Uncle Tom’s Cabin’
item.summary: After 42 years of slavery, Josiah Henson escaped to Canada, where he wrote a memoir, founded a school and led others to freedom. But his home long bore the name “Uncle Tom,” to the offense of many.

item.title: A Hotel in Venezuela’s Capital Has Become the U.S. Embassy’s De Facto Headquarters
item.summary: The J.W. Marriott in Venezuela’s capital is suddenly awash in U.S. diplomats, spies and fortune seekers, showcasing changes in the country.

item.title: Japan’s Takaichi Pitches Strength and Stability in Visits to Australia and Vietnam
item.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is attempting to raise Japan’s profile at a time when China’s clout is rising and doubts about the United States are spreading.

item.title: 3 People Are Evacuated From Cruise Ship With Hantavirus Outbreak
item.summary: Three people with possible symptoms of the disease were evacuated on Wednesday morning from the Dutch-flagged MV Hondius.

item.title: World Cup Dynamic Ticket Pricing Drives Argentine Soccer Fans To Extremes
item.summary: Dynamic ticket pricing has made this year’s tournament the most expensive in history, pushing Argentine fans to extremes.

item.title: Leo XIV Is the First Pope From the U.S. He’s Making That an Asset.
item.summary: A year into his papacy, Leo has shown a readiness to challenge Washington, defying any concerns about the election of an American pontiff.
